clutchserve

Do the greats really serve better when it matters most? The goal for clutchserve is to allow tennis fanatics who want to put the term “clutch” to the test. It packages point-by-point data on men’s professional matches with an interactive dashboard to compare how players serve on pressure points (break points and optionally deuce) with how they serve on every other point. You can also visualise a player’s progression over time to see whether they’ve become more clutch across their career.

Website: https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-pang0023-arch/

Installation

You can install the development version of clutchserve from GitHub with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-pang0023-arch")

Launch the app 

clutchserve::run_app()

The app shows every player as a dot on a funnel chart, compared with a typical player. Use the sidebar to filter by surface, years and choose what counts as a reliable pressure point and set that as the minimum number of pressure points. Click a player to see how their serve under pressure has changed over time.

Example

pressure_gap() summarises each player’s point performance across all their matches (including pressure points and normal points).

library(clutchserve)

pressure_gap(serve_pressure) |>
  head()
#> # A tibble: 6 × 12
#>   player         matches pressure_pts pressure_won serve_pts serve_won other_pts
#>   <chr>            <int>        <dbl>        <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 Roger Federer      722         3437         2266     59860     41465     56423
#> 2 Novak Djokovic     550         3119         1996     45548     30468     42429
#> 3 Rafael Nadal       424         2598         1659     34693     22879     32095
#> 4 Andy Murray        256         1810         1093     21876     13906     20066
#> 5 Hubert Hurkacz     319         1624         1082     26464     18056     24840
#> 6 Daniil Medved…     284         1579          997     22372     14786     20793
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: other_won <dbl>, pressure_pct <dbl>, other_pct <dbl>,
#> #   gap <dbl>, reliable <lgl>

Data

serve_pressure has one row per player per recorded match: 14,570 rows of men’s matches from 1990 onwards. It comes from Match Charting Project by Jeff Sackmann, licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The packaged data carries the same licence. The script that downloads and cleans it is in data-raw/serve_pressure.R.

The matches are recorded by volunteers, so famous players and big matches are overrepresented. Results describe the recorded matches, not every match a player has played. This data should not be taken as a random sample of professional tennis.
